subject: Alerting & On-call — renewal options and procurement path
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@pagerflux.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: contracts@pagerflux.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal quote and multi-year options for PagerFlux alerting

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our discussion, attached is v3 of the renewal quote that includes two changes you asked for: a burst-capacity add-on for sustained spikes, and a 10% credit for consolidating Statuspage-like incident pages into our hosted status product.

Highlights: 
- 24/7 directional on-call support (chat + escalations) included in Pro plan
- Burstable capacity: +30% throughput for 6 hours/day at negotiated rate
- 3-year committed pricing: 18% discount on list

I've attached PagerFlux-Quote-v3.pdf and a breakdown of estimated token/event volumes. Happy to walk the team through the figures — proposing a quick call Thursday morning if that works for you.

Best,
Sam Jenkins
Head of Customer Success, PagerFlux
(attachment: PagerFlux-Quote-v3.pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal quote and multi-year options for PagerFlux alerting

Looping you all in — Sam sent the updated quote. Quick read: the burst add-on looks useful for holiday traffic and model rollout days, but I want procurement and platform ops to weigh in on SLO implications and contract terms.

Key asks: 
- Laura: can procurement review the commercial terms and flag any unusual indemnities or auto-renew clauses?
- Dylan: can you validate the technical assumptions (KV cache / ingestion rates) against our redwood-alerting-usage.csv?
- Monica: assess whether the hosted status pages fit our compliance needs vs. self-hosted option.

Proposed next steps: internal sync tomorrow 11am PT, then follow-up with PagerFlux on Thursday if we have consensus.

Thanks,
Markus
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote and multi-year options for PagerFlux alerting

Thanks Markus — quick procurement read below after skimming the PDF and SOW draft.

Red flags / negotiation targets: 
- Auto-renew: the clause rolls forward on anniversary unless 60 days notice; push to 30 days and require price-rise caps if we commit multi-year.
- Data residency: their hosted status pages mention EU region hosting as "available upon request" — need firm SLA or keep a self-hosted contingency.
- Termination for convenience: propose a 180-day wind-down (we need time to migrate if service degraded).

Vendor concessions to ask for: 
- A 90-day trial at reduced rates to validate ingestion patterns (no penalty).
- A paragraph confirming SOC2 Type II evidence sharing cadence.

I can draft the redlines and loop legal after our internal sync. Also flagged a discrepancy between the usage estimate and our redwood-alerting-usage.csv (PagerFlux is ~25% higher on event volume). Dylan, can you confirm their numbers?

Laura
Sr. Procurement Manager

(attachment: SOW-draft-2027-04.docx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood-inference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood-inference.com>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@pagerflux.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T15:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote and multi-year options for PagerFlux alerting

Markus / team / Sam — quick technical follow-up after I ran the usage CSV through the event model: PagerFlux's baseline ingest matches our peak-light estimate, but their retention assumptions are optimistic. Practically:

- If we enable burst capacity during model rollouts, expect sustained KV usage to increase by ~18% for 48 hours. The burst add-on covers the TPS but not retention costs.
- Recommendation: accept the burst feature for 6-month pilot, but cap the pilot to three "rollout events" and instrument with a cost alert tied to the daily retention footprint.
- For status pages: hosted product meets our display needs but misses our audit export format (they export CSV only). If we require immutable archives for audits, push for S3-compatible export or plan for on-prem archive.

Sam — appreciate the quick turnaround. If PagerFlux can add a clause about SOC2 evidence and a 30-day export API commitment, procurement is willing to move to a short-term committed contract while we build the archive automation.

Dylan
Principal Reliability Engineer
(attachment: redwood-alerting-usage.csv)
